other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 2988, Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act

summary: H.R. 2988, the Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act, amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to set new rules for how fiduciaries manage employer-sponsored retirement plans. The bill requires investment decisions to be based strictly on financial and economic factors, prohibits discrimination when choosing service providers, outlines standards for exercising shareholder rights and proxy voting, and requires specific warnings and notices for participants using brokerage windows or self-directed accounts.

affected_groups.effect: Must alter investment evaluation criteria to focus strictly on pecuniary factors, follow anti-discrimination rules for service providers, manage proxy voting under new guidelines, and ensure brokerage window participants receive mandatory notices.
Will see changes in how plan investments and proxies are managed, and must review and acknowledge risk and fee warnings before executing trades through brokerage windows or self-directed options.
Subject to non-discrimination mandates when being selected or retained, and monitored for compliance with economic-interest and proxy-voting standards.
affected_groups.group: Plan Service Providers and Investment Managers

key_provisions: Requires plan fiduciaries to make investment decisions based solely on pecuniary factors, preventing them from sacrificing returns or taking on extra risk to promote non-pecuniary goals.

Allows non-pecuniary factors to be used only as a tie-breaker when alternative investments are equal on pecuniary grounds, or when selecting options for participant-directed plans under specific conditions.
Prohibits plan fiduciaries from discriminating based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin when selecting, monitoring, or retaining service providers, counselors, or other fiduciaries.
Clarifies that managing shareholder rights and voting proxies must be done solely in the economic interest of participants, but does not require voting on every proxy.
Provides a safe harbor for fiduciaries adopting specific proxy-voting policies, such as refraining from voting when plan assets in an issuer fall below 5 percent.
Requires participants using non-designated investment arrangements, such as brokerage windows, to receive and acknowledge a specific warning notice and growth illustration before making trades.
Directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a study comparing returns from brokerage accounts and similar arrangements with other plan investment options within two years.
missing_information: The official text does not state the specific financial penalties or enforcement mechanisms for fiduciaries who fail to comply with the new requirements.
The source material does not provide estimates of the total administrative cost or economic savings resulting from the mandated notices and policy changes.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 2988, the Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act, amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to set new rules for how fiduciaries manage employer-sponsored retirement plans. The bill requires investment decisions to be based strictly on financial and economic factors, prohibits discrimination when choosing service providers, outlines standards for exercising shareholder rights and proxy voting, and requires specific warnings and notices for participants using brokerage windows or self-directed accounts.
summary_detail.significance: The bill updates federal standards governing private-sector retirement plans by enforcing strict economic considerations for investments, limiting non-financial goals, and increasing disclosures for self-directed brokerage accounts. It affects administrative duties for the managers of pension and retirement assets subject to ERISA.
